resources.string: Guidance tool for a clinician-approved plan. Not a medical device. Sensors estimate body-segment movement, never vertebral positions or nerve compression.
• C6 lesion: repeat MRI per radiologist — set your date in the notes below
• RED FLAGS — stop exercising and seek urgent care: arm weakness, worsening numbness, hand clumsiness, balance/walking problems, bowel/bladder changes

What sensors can and cannot measure
CAN: body-segment angles, movement tempo, reps, posture trends, activity, sleep position (bed mat).
CANNOT: vertebral positions, disc protrusions, nerve compression, C6 lesion stability — imaging only.
1. Log your current pillow + mattress tonight (pillow type, height, position you wake in).
2. Rate morning neck pain and arm symptoms each day (Home tab check-in).
3. Trial ONE change at a time (e.g. adjustable-height pillow) for ≥3 nights before judging.
4. Side sleeping: pillow should fill the shoulder-to-head gap without tilting the head up.
5. Back sleeping: support the neck curve without pushing the chin toward the chest.
6. Avoid stomach sleeping — it holds the neck rotated for long periods.
• Bed pressure mat (FSR array or commercial) under the mattress → back/side/stomach + turns.
• Upper-trunk IMU node worn in a shirt pocket → orientation + turning events.
• Smartwatch via Health Connect → sleep windows + movement (imported, not diagnostic).
The app reports position CLASS with uncertainty; it never claims to know your neck angle at 3am.
Start with an adjustable-height pillow before buying an expensive mattress.
